{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./job_wgpu.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from Slurm:
#   --time=00:10:00   -> -t 10m
#   --gres=gpu:1      -> -g 1
#   -c 4              -> -c 4
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 4 -g 1 -t 10m --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  # NOTE: Slurm --job-name=job_wgpu not translated.
  # Performance/ops implication: job identification may be less convenient; runtime performance is unaffected.

  # NOTE: Slurm --open-mode=append not translated.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: output files may be overwritten instead of appended depending on defaults.

  # NOTE: Slurm --output/--error use %j/%x expansions which Flux does not provide portably.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: log filenames may not be unique unless you add uniqueness.

  # NOTE: Slurm --export=ALL not translated.
  # Performance implication: usually none (Flux typically inherits the environment), but if your site sanitizes environments, missing exports could change runtime behavior.

  # NOTE: Slurm --mem=64G not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a memory reservation/limit, the job may contend for memory or be OOM-killed, affecting reliability/performance.

  flux run -n 1 -c 4 -g 1 \
    singularity exec --nv \
      --overlay "$SCRATCH/overlay-50G-10M.ext3:ro" \
      /scratch/work/public/singularity/cuda10.1-cudnn7-devel-ubuntu18.04-20201207.sif \
      /bin/bash -c '
        source /ext3/env.sh
        conda activate
        python ./test_gpu.py
      '
fi
"
}
